head: 85c07b7c929f7c0b3c913b70457fe08bf52ace8b
summary: Substantively clean implementation. All 5 issue closures landed; refactor preserves canonical bytes + public surface; tests pass (43/43); clippy/fmt/doc all green. Two MINOR findings: dead-code residue of the now-unused parse_err helper, and stale line-number citations in the parse_err_at + #934 doc-comments. Both safe to land; both should be fixed inline before/at merge per HARD RULE 12 'inline trivial fixes' clause + CLAUDE.md rule 5 'no deprecated aliases — delete, don't comment'. No BLOCKER, no MAJOR.

findings.title: Dead-code residue: `Parser::parse_err` helper is unused after the #760 migration
findings.evidence: All 10 bare `self.parse_err(...)` callsites on base (e89a1919, 10 callsites verified) were migrated to `parse_err_at(start_line, start_col, ...)`. Post-migration: 0 `self.parse_err(` callsites + the helper definition at src/lib.rs:776-783 remains. `RUSTFLAGS='-W dead_code' cargo build -p benten-dsl-compiler` emits `warning: method 'parse_err' is never used --> crates/benten-dsl-compiler/src/lib.rs:776:8`. Workspace `[lints]` does not escalate dead_code to deny, which is why CI clippy didn't catch it. The doccomment on `parse_err_at` line 785 still references `[\`Self::parse_err\`]` so deleting `parse_err` requires updating that reference (sharpen to 'span-anchored helper for emitting CompileError::Parse with a captured span').
findings.disposition_rationale: HARD RULE 12 + CLAUDE.md rule 5 'No deprecated aliases or backward-compat shims. Fresh project. Delete, don't comment.' Trivial inline fix; orchestrator can apply directly (5-line delete + 2-line doc tweak). Not a BLOCKER because the dead helper doesn't break runtime correctness, and `dead_code` is workspace-warning not deny.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete lines 776-783 (the `parse_err` method body); update `parse_err_at` doccomment line 785 from '[\`Self::parse_err\`]' to 'companion to per-site Diagnostic construction'.

findings.title: Stale line-number citations in two doc-comments (parse_err_at + #934 numeric comment)
findings.evidence: Two doccomment blocks reference line numbers that don't match the post-PR source. (1) Line 599 comment cites '`parse_identifier` (line 638)' and 'read_until_balanced (line 682)' — actual locations are 678 and 740. (2) Line 791-792 doccomment cites 'parse_identifier (line 638-656)' and 'parse_primitive (line 367-368)' — actual locations are 678 and 417. The cite-drift CI detector (scripts/drift-detect.ts) does not match `line NNN` plain-prose patterns so this would not have been auto-caught, but it falls squarely in the §3.5g cross-doc-cite-drift class (pim-N origin pattern). A future reader following any of these cites will land in unrelated code 40-260 lines away.
findings.disposition_rationale: HARD RULE 12 + pim-1 §3.5b post-fix doc-coupling pre-flight. Inline orchestrator fix; sharpen each citation to either correct lines or symbol-only (`parse_identifier` / `read_until_balanced` / `parse_primitive` without line numbers, since the symbol-only form is drift-free by construction).
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `(line 638)` / `(line 682)` / `(line 367-368)` / `(line 638-656)` with bare symbol names (`parse_identifier` / `read_until_balanced` / `parse_primitive`). The symbol references are drift-free; the line numbers add no information given the symbol is named.

findings.evidence: INTERNALS.md line 48 says 'src/lib.rs (894 lines)'; post-PR the file is 1356 lines (parse_helper-extraction + 13 closure-pin tests). INTERNALS.md line 5 last-refresh annotation is still '@ 8141b94 (Phase-4-Foundation tag-eve, 2026-05-14)' — chunk-2's edits + the prior chunk-1 edits are not reflected. Implementer touched only the §6 Benches inventory subsection; §3 file inventory + §1 'whole crate is 894 LOC' + §4 'public-item count' framing should also retense.
findings.destination: Carry as part of the next G-CORE-DSL chunk merge OR a post-batch INTERNALS.md retense pass; not BLOCKER because the document is internal-audit-only and explicit-line-count drift is a known recurring doc-coupling pattern in this crate (the same Cargo.toml '~200-300 LOC, 4 public items' framing in INTERNALS.md §4 is called out as an Open Question item 1 already). Orchestrator-direct option: pre-merge bump the §3 line count + §5 last-refresh SHA inline.
findings.disposition_rationale: OBSERVATION rather than MINOR-FIX-NOW because this drift class is already named in the document itself (§9 Open Questions item 1) + falls into the routine 'retense INTERNALS.md every wave that touches the crate' rhythm. Inline orchestrator bump preferred if cheap; otherwise carry to the next chunk's retense.

rubric_dispositions.1_coverage_completeness: APPROVE — 13 closure-pin tests exercise the SUBSTANTIVE production arms per pim-18 §3.6f. Each pin has would-FAIL evidence in its doccomment (regression of slice start = wrong value / regression of byte arithmetic = chain split / etc). No aspirational-prose gaps detected.

rubric_dispositions.3_934_numeric_slicing: APPROVE — Int/Float/negative/`$`-prefix preservation all verified by closure pins. parse_string correctly excluded (the inline #934 comment names the escape-decoding hard-stop). Negative-int test confirms `start` captured BEFORE the `if c == '-'` advance, preserving the leading sign in the slice window.
rubric_dispositions.4_931_peek_at_deletion: APPROVE — base verification: baseline grep `peek_at` returned exactly 2 hits (1 callsite + 1 definition). Post-PR: 0 callsites + 0 definition (only 3 documentation references remain, all in comments referring to the prior code). Byte-comparison correctness: both `-` (0x2D) and `>` (0x3E) are ASCII so `bytes.get(self.pos) == Some(&b'-')` is equivalent to the prior char-comparison.
rubric_dispositions.5_760_parse_err_at_helper: APPROVE — all 10 bare `parse_err` callsites migrated to `parse_err_at` (counted: lines 556, 620, 625, 635, 642, 668, 708, 730, 732, 765). Each callsite captures `(start_line, start_col)` BEFORE the fallible consume so the diagnostic anchors at the offending span start. Closure pins verify unterminated-string anchors at opening-quote line (not at end-of-input cursor) — the most behavior-substantive of the migrations. See finding dsl-c2-r5-mr-1: the now-unused `parse_err` helper should be deleted, not retained.

Behavior preservation verified by issue_663_all_12_primitive_kinds_dispatch_via_helpers + the existing permuted_keys_yield_identical_canonical_bytes + canonical_bytes_v1_scheme_pin tests (3/3 pass). Note: `parse_paren_string_optional_object` skips ws only inside the `Some` branch before expect_char(')'); the `None` branch falls through with cursor already at the post-string skip_ws position — correct.
